runs.title: Q3 Revenue Summary (Product Lines)
runs.body:
Subject: Q3 Revenue Summary (Product Lines)

Hi [Sales Director],

Overall, Q3 revenue increased year over year across our three product lines. Total Q3 2025 revenue is 2,620,000 EUR (up from 2,250,000 EUR in Q3 2024), a gain of 370,000 EUR.

Strongest and weakest performers in Q3 2025:
- Strongest: Core — 1,240,000 EUR
- Analytics — 880,000 EUR
- Weakest: Connect — 410,000 EUR

On a year-over-year basis, Core rose from 1,100,000 EUR to 1,240,000 EUR and Analytics increased from 700,000 EUR to 880,000 EUR. Connect declined from 450,000 EUR to 410,000 EUR.

If helpful, I can follow up with a brief sales-focused view of what’s most likely contributing to the Core and Analytics lift versus the Connect softness.

judge_scores.justification: The email leads with the overall Q3 2025 result, names the strongest (Core) and weakest (Connect) lines, includes total Q3 2025 revenue, and presents clear per-line figures in a professional, analytical structure with only minor opportunities to tighten wording.

judge_scores.justification: The artefact accurately reports all funnel stage counts and conversion rates (including the offer-to-hire percentage), clearly highlights the largest drop-off early in the funnel, and presents the information in a neutral, leadership-suitable, well-structured one-page format with only minor opportunity to tighten wording.

runs.title: Q3 2025 Hiring Funnel—Leadership One-Page Report
runs.body:
Q3 2025 Hiring Funnel (Leadership Team Summary)

Across the quarter, the hiring funnel moved from 1,450 applications to 230 interviews, then to 48 offers, culminating in 35 hires.

Conversion rates:
• Applications → Interviews: 230/1,450 ≈ 15.9%.
• Interviews → Offers: 48/230 ≈ 20.9%.
• Offers → Hires: 35/48 ≈ 72.9%.

Largest drop-off:
The most significant decline occurs early in the funnel, from 1,450 applications to 230 interviews. This is a reduction of 1,220 candidates (about an 84.1% drop), indicating that screening and initial qualification drive most of the volume loss.

Near-final-stage efficiency:
Once candidates reach the offer stage, closing and onboarding execution appear comparatively effective, with 35 hires achieved from 48 offers (about 72.9%).

Overall result:
The quarter produced 35 hires from 1,450 applications, an end-to-end conversion of about 2.4%.

judge_scores.justification: The artefact accurately presents all funnel counts, highlights the largest drop-off (applications→interviews) with volume and percent decline, adds the requested offer-to-hire conversion rate, and is neatly structured in a neutral leadership-summary tone, with only minor opportunities to tighten wording for a strictly one-page cadence.

runs.title: Q3 2025 Hiring Funnel — Leadership Pre-Read
runs.body:
Q3 2025 Hiring Funnel (Leadership Summary)

Hiring progressed from 1,450 applications to 230 interviews, 48 offers, and 35 hires. Overall conversion from applications to hires was 2.4% (35/1,450), indicating substantial drop-off early in the process.

Largest drop-off: applications to interviews. This stage reduced candidates from 1,450 to 230—a loss of 1,220 candidates, or 84.1%. While subsequent stages also tightened the funnel, the biggest volume reduction occurred before interviews.

For context, interview-to-offer conversion was 20.9% (48/230), and offer-to-hire conversion was 72.9% (35/48). This suggests that once candidates reach interviews, the later stages are comparatively efficient.

Leadership takeaway: focus attention on the front end of the funnel to improve throughput from applications to interviews, while maintaining the relatively strong conversion seen in later steps.
